target_customer: Teenagers and young adults in Brazil, with parents as consent holders
problem: Teens had no bank account designed for them to learn money skills and receive earnings from jobs and small businesses.
business_model: digital account and prepaid card with interchange; subscription of about 2 USD per month until late 2021, then a free core account

founders.name: Joao Pedro Thompson
founders.background_notes: YC page: investment banking at Itau BBA and finance at Kraft Heinz where he headed LatAm treasury.

founders.name: Thiago Achatz
founders.background_notes: YC page: part of the founding teams of Rappi (YC W16) and Grow (Grin YC S18 and Yellow).

founders.name: Mateus Craveiro
founders.background_notes: YC page: Principal Software Engineer at Pagar.me.

founders.name: Sophie Secaf
founders.background_notes: YC page: creative strategist, political researcher in Sao Paulo, led NYC branding company YONE, co-founded the YAGA festival.

exit.reason: Z1 CEO said a new fundraising was considered in 2025 but NG.Cash opportunity made more sense; founders did not take roles at NG.CASH

competitors.name: Next (Bradesco)
competitors.what: Digital bank launched in 2017 aimed at younger customers

competitors.name: Nubank
competitors.what: Dominant Brazilian digital bank with an interest in teenage customers

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs payment institution licensing, card issuing and Pix integration plus child safety flows, standard fintech engineering with regulatory work.

defensibility.rationale: Payment institution authorization helps, but large banks and Nubank could serve teens and the brand was the main differentiator.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Itau entered the young segment according to a headline on NG.CASH; NG.CASH absorbed Z1's customer base in early 2025.

market_need_then: Brazilian teens lacked bank accounts; the company had a large TikTok following of about 400,000 per an undated article and launched its product in January 2021 per Insper.

branding.name_origin: Derived from Gen Z, the generation it targets, per a Suno article.

identity.visual_style: pop aesthetic aimed at Gen Z
identity.voice_and_tone: Casual, humorous Brazilian Portuguese using informal words; talks to teens not parents.

branding.brand_signature: Positioning as a Gen Z brand and humorous TikTok content

rebrands.why: Z1 users were moved to NG.CASH accounts when it took over the customer base; Z1 brand ceased.

branding.community_and_virality: About 400,000 TikTok followers per an undated Brazilian article and use of Gen Z creators, per Suno.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear Gen Z positioning with a large social following and a CMO from a branding background, but the brand ceased after the customer base transferred.

pivots.from: Paid subscription teen account at about 2 USD per month
pivots.to: Free core banking with a broader Gen Z positioning including customers from 18
pivots.why: Announced with the Series A to grow the base.

outcome_analysis: Z1 raised a 2.5M seed from Homebrew and a 10M Series A led by Kaszek in November 2021 on a Gen Z branding strategy, then went free on its core account. After about four years as a standalone service its customer base was absorbed by NG.CASH in early 2025 and the brand ended. The CEO said a new round was considered but NG.CASH made more sense, and the founders did not join, so this is a customer base transfer rather than a celebrated exit; terms were not found.
notes: Directory status is Active but the Z1 site says users are moving into NG.CASH, so this conflicts. The exit type acquisition is used for the customer base transfer; amount undisclosed. A Portuguese report gives R$54M (about 10.4M USD) co-led by Homebrew, Parade Ventures and Kindred Ventures, and a R$55M Series A led by Kaszek, and a R$14M seed led by Homebrew; lead attributions conflict. The 2.5M USD seed amount comes from coverage that the 10M Series A came six months after 2.5M USD; the July 2021 TechCrunch article is cited for date and lead. Founding year 2019 per fintech coverage; some sources say 2020 or 2021. Competitor entries come from undated general Brazilian banking articles. Failure factors are my judgment from the CEO statement and are not explicit in a source. Education not found for any founder.
